issues.title: FHI "Threshold" column made a required report element, contradicting charter disclaimers
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Actually found and reported by @ayourtch (Andrew Yourtchenko) in his review of the -03 draft set (Major finding [F13]):

Table 6 (Fabric Health Indicators) gives every indicator a literal numeric "Threshold" (CPU < 30%, Memory < 70%, FEC < 1e-12, CRC errors = 0, 0 routing flaps, 100% QP active, PCIe BW > 90%), and Table 10 makes that table a required report element. This is acceptance-criteria-shaped content, contradicting the BMWG-charter disclaimers elsewhere in the document. The training document's own FHI table, correctly, has no thresholds.

Fix: renamed the column to an informative "Typical Healthy Range" with a charter disclaimer, and softened the reporting requirement to reflect the column is informative, not pass/fail — mirroring the pattern training-bench's own FHI table already uses.

issues.title: Test 5.4 storage-tier paths never state whether the peer is remote
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Actually found and reported by @ayourtch (Andrew Yourtchenko) in his review of the -03 draft set (Major finding [F18]):

Test 5.4's storage-tier paths (GPU HBM to CPU DRAM / NVMe) never state whether the peer is remote. A local (same-node) transfer is pure intra-node PCIe with zero DUT/fabric involvement, and TERMINOLOGY Section 1.2 excludes storage networking from scope.

Fix: restricted every tier pair to explicitly remote (fabric-traversing) peers, and added a note that same-node tier pairs are out of scope.

issues.title: Appendix D opcode error: 0x0B mislabeled as "RDMA WRITE Last with Immediate Data"
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Actually found and reported by @ayourtch (Andrew Yourtchenko) in his review of the -03 draft set (Major finding [F20]):

Appendix D's segmented-WRITE description says the last packet "carries OpCode ... 0x0B (RDMA WRITE Last with Immediate Data)". Per the IBTA RC opcode table, Last-with-Immediate is actually 0x09; 0x0B is Only-with-Immediate, a single-packet opcode that cannot terminate a First/Middle sequence (a conformant responder would NAK it). The with-immediate variants also carry a 4-byte ImmDt field missing from the frame layout.

Verified directly against the Linux kernel's canonical IB opcode header (include/rdma/ib_pack.h) before fixing: 0x09 = RDMA_WRITE_LAST_WITH_IMMEDIATE, 0x0B = RDMA_WRITE_ONLY_WITH_IMMEDIATE.

Fix: corrected the opcode to 0x09, added a note explaining why 0x0B doesn't apply here, and added the missing 4B ImmDt row to the frame table (present only for the with-immediate opcode variants, positioned after the payload).

issues.title: Topology C means something different here than in training-bench
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
We say the training document's topologies still apply, then define Topology C as Disaggregated Prefill/Decode. Training-bench uses Topology C for Rail-Optimized.

Found by @ayourtch in his -03 review (F103).

issues.title: ITL test can't produce the 10,000 samples it asks for
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
The procedure submits a single request of ~2048 output tokens, which yields at most 2,047 inter-token gaps. The measurement section then asks for at least 10,000 samples per condition.

Needs repetition or concurrency, and the count should be reported.

Found by @ayourtch in his -03 review (F97).

issues.title: Appendix E example cites an architecture whose top-k doesn't match
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
The worked example computes with M3 (k=2) but describes it as representative of a well-known MoE architecture. That architecture's published top-k is 8, which is row M4. With k=8 the numbers are roughly 4x.

Either switch to M4 or drop the attribution.

Found by @ayourtch in his -03 review (F34).

issues.title: TTFT_fabric reference value is 60% of the whole TTFT budget
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Appendix B lists TTFT < 500 ms P99 and TTFT_fabric < 300 ms P99. That leaves 40% for everything else, including prefill, which the document elsewhere says dominates TTFT.

Found by @ayourtch in his -03 review (F39).

issues.title: GPU-NIC PCIe health indicator measures an out-of-scope segment
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Section 1.2 puts the GPU-to-NIC PCIe path out of scope, but it's listed as a Fabric Health Indicator. It's genuinely useful as context (a starved PCIe link looks like a slow fabric), so probably worth keeping if labelled as such.

Found by @ayourtch in his -03 review (F96).

issues.title: Wide-EP scaling efficiency formula has a spurious N/8 factor
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body: Andrew caught (F19) that the scaling efficiency formula in Wide Expert Parallelism Scaling, (EP=8 latency)/(EP=N latency) × (N/8), doesn't hold up — dropped the N/8 factor and switched the baseline to EP=16, the first configuration that actually requires inter-node fabric communication (EP=8 is intra-node only).

issues.title: AllToAll Dispatch Throughput heatmap has no data to plot
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body: Andrew noticed (F21) that the Reporting Format for AllToAll Dispatch Throughput calls for a heatmap with EP group size and batch size as axes, but the Procedure never actually sweeps either — it just runs a fixed config row. Added the sweep so there's something to put in the heatmap.

issues.title: Primary Throughput KPIs table mixes in a cache-hit rate and a fairness index
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body: Andrew pointed out (F87) that "Primary Throughput KPIs" contains Prefix_cache_hit_rate and JFI_decode, neither of which is a throughput metric. Renamed the section/table to "Primary Throughput and Efficiency KPIs" and clarified that JFI_decode is actually three separate per-metric Jain's Fairness Index values (KV cache receive rate, GPU utilization, output TPS), not one combined index — the original wording read like a single composite metric.

issues.title: KV_xfer_latency DUT tag is missing DUT-PD
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body: Andrew found (F91) that KV_xfer_latency is tagged DUT-N only in the Fabric-Level KPIs table, but DUT-N, DUT-PD in the KPI-to-Test Mapping Summary later in the doc — and the T_transfer prose elsewhere confirms DUT-PD is a real measurement point for this KPI. Aligned the two tables.

issues.title: Fabric Scale Limits 10% threshold reads like a pass/fail criterion
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body: Same charter-scope issue Andrew raised elsewhere (F38): "Identify the scale limit as the point where any KPI degrades by more than 10%" reads as a hard requirement. Reframed as an illustrative reporting point with the same charter disclaimer used for the Fabric Health Indicators table.

pulls.title: Editorial pass: address Andrew Yourtchenko's review + acronym/inclusive-language cleanup
pulls.author: cpignata
pulls.body:
## Summary

Addresses the minor and editorial issues identified by Andrew Yourtchenko in his review of the draft set (-03), plus a broader editorial pass covering acronym consistency, inclusive language, and idnits hygiene.

- Fixed a genuine leaked-markup bug: CFG-E's blank-fill underscores were being silently swallowed by Markdown emphasis parsing, dropping content from the rendered table cell (verified against the actual HTML/XML output, not just suspected)
- Fixed a garbled negative-scope sentence in the Scope and Applicability section and a stale cross-reference for the DUT boundary diagram
- Fixed the RFC 2544 misattribution of a "minimum 20 trials" convention that RFC 2544 doesn't actually define
- Fixed a wrong Appendix E traffic aggregate that included 672 intra-node GPU pairs that never cross the fabric (corrected from ~700 MB to the fabric-visible ~648 MB)
- Fixed the IB-path-MTU-vs-Ethernet-MTU conflation in the frame format notes
- Reference list fixes: added the missing RFC 8239, reclassified RFC 2889/6349 from normative to informative (mentioned once, never substantively relied on), added proper IBTA-ROCE and DeepEP citations
- Fixed Expert Parallelism (EP) capitalization inconsistency and Jain's Fairness Index's missing possessive
- Harmonized the 24-hour soak-test sampling interval and IANA Considerations wording with the companion documents (was 15x apart: 60s vs 15min)
- Standardized multiplication notation to × and switched <=/>= to ≤/≥; centered the topology figure
- Reviewed for NIST IR 8366 inclusive-language guidance (replaced "hang" with "stop responding")
- Added Andrew Yourtchenko's review credit to Acknowledgments

comments.author: cpignata
comments.body: @ayourtch would appreciate your review here as well — thank you for the thorough review of the -03 draft set, several of these commits address findings from it directly.

pulls.title: Fix three Major findings from Andrew Yourtchenko's review
pulls.author: cpignata
pulls.body:
## Summary

Fixes the three Major findings from Andrew Yourtchenko's review of the -03 draft set that weren't included in the earlier editorial PR (#28, already merged).

- FHI "Threshold" column was a required report element, contradicting the charter's acceptance-criteria disclaimers; relabeled to an informative "Typical Healthy Range" with a disclaimer, mirroring the pattern training-bench's own FHI table already uses. Closes #29
- Test 5.4's storage-tier paths never stated whether the peer was remote; a local (same-node) transfer would be pure intra-node PCIe with zero DUT/fabric involvement. Restricted every tier pair to explicitly remote and noted local pairs are out of scope. Closes #30
- Appendix D mislabeled OpCode 0x0B as "RDMA WRITE Last with Immediate Data" for a segmented sequence; verified against the Linux kernel's canonical IB opcode header (0x09 = WRITE Last with Immediate, 0x0B = WRITE Only with Immediate, a single-packet opcode that cannot terminate a First/Middle sequence) and corrected the opcode. Also added the missing 4B ImmDt field. Closes #31

reviews.author: fcalabri
reviews.body:
corrections made to the Appendix D Frame Format Table:
- OpCode 0x0B has been identified as “RDMA Write Only With Immediate Data” and is applicable to one packet reference frame, and removed the incorrect text indicating that it terminated a segmented sequence. This was actually done by OpCode 0x09.

- The 4 byte ImmDt field has been moved into its appropriate position within an IBTA frame format. It is now located between RETH and the payload, rather than immediately following the payload. The offsets have also been modified based on this movement (the payload will begin at offset 78/98 when including ImmDt or 74/94 when not including ImmDt).

- A note has been added describing segmented transfer headers. RETH is included only once, in the first packet of a segmented transfer (OpCode = 0x06). In the last packet of a segmented transfer (OpCode = 0x09), ImmDt is carried directly after the BTH with no RETH.

- The MoE All-To-All worked example had the earlier intra-node/inter-node pair split. The all-to-all aggregate size for the fabric has been modified to approximately 646 MB (prefill) and approximately 20.2 MB (decode); the decode bandwidth has been modified from 45 GB/s to approximately 41 GB/s. The derivation (61 x ~20.2 MB / 30 ms) is contained inline. The original figure was using the pre-split 9,120-pair number

pulls.title: Third pass on Andrew's -03 review
pulls.author: cpignata
pulls.body:
Five more from Andrew's review.

- Renamed our Topology C to Topology D. Training-bench uses Topology C for Rail-Optimized, and we say its topologies still apply. Closes #33
- ITL test asked for 10,000 samples from a single 2048-token request, which gives at most 2,047. Repeat and report the count. Closes #34
- Dropped the architecture attribution from the Appendix E example; that architecture's top-k is 8 (row M4), not the k=2 we compute with. Kept the M3 numbers. Closes #35
- TTFT_fabric was 300 ms against a 500 ms TTFT budget. Expressed as a fraction instead. Closes #36
- Labelled the GPU-NIC PCIe indicator contextual, since that segment is outside the DUT boundary. Closes #37

reviews.author: fcalabri
reviews.body:
- Section 7.1 (F04): the formula intro still said "dispatch payload per GPU per
  MoE layer"; T_dispatch is a per-source-destination-pair quantity (as Table 7
  and the MoE appendix already state), so the label is corrected. Added the
  per-accelerator egress formula T_egress = B × k × H_model × P_bytes × (N-1)/N
  (= T_dispatch × (N-1)), with a note that only inter-node peers are
  fabric-visible (88 of 95 in the appendix worked example). Closes the
  per-pair/per-accelerator ambiguity.

- MoE appendix (F04/F92 follow-up): per-pair value aligned to ~76.5 KB (exact:
  76,458 B) so the bullet matches the aggregate line and 76.5 KB × 8,448 ≈
  646 MB recomputes from the printed numbers.
